Hand it here and get out of here.
I understood, you are busy in here.
Yes, just do not tell anyone.
You offend me, Viktor Petrovich.
You and I are men, after all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of total nonsense is this?
Now we will think of something, Chef.
Timur, what have you done here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'happened', paired with 'случаться'.

examples.trans: What happened?
Nothing will happen.

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Timur, what have you done here?
And what are you doing here?
It seems we did not get caught here.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тут женщина шампанское в номер заказала.
examples.trans: A woman ordered champagne to the room here.
Then what woman ordered champagne?
She is a wise woman.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'champagne' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тут женщина шампанское в номер заказала.
examples.trans: A woman ordered champagne to the room here.
Then what woman ordered champagne?
Open the champagne!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, Viktor Petrovich.
I am inspecting your restaurant.
Is everything alright with you?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'number' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хотите пойти к себе в номер?
examples.trans: Do you want to go to your room?

examples.text: Тут женщина шампанское в номер заказала.
examples.trans: A woman ordered champagne to the room here.
People are tied up in the room over there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Тут женщина шампанское в номер заказала.
examples.trans: A woman ordered champagne to the room here.
Maybe we should order?
We ordered tea and sandwiches.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Let us make a bet then.
Let us test it right now!
Enough, let us sort this out calmly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Let me go from here, please.
Hello, did my husband stop by here?
No, he did not come in here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
Hello, Viktor Petrovich.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: I'm going home.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'сюда').

examples.trans: Let me go from here, please.
That is it, go away from here quickly.
Hand it here and get out of here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
I am inspecting your restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understood', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: I understood everything, Chef!
And now I have understood everything.
I understood, you are busy in here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just do not worry.
You will not withstand a blow from a coconut.
I will not withstand such a blow?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нятый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('busy').

examples.trans: I understood, you are busy in here.
It's occupied.
I'm busy right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yes, it is just so unexpected.
A coconut has already fallen on me.
You will not withstand a blow from a coconut.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just do not worry.
Brother, just do not worry!
Yes, just do not tell anyone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'anyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Coconuts never warn you in advance.
I locked him in the refrigerator.
Chef, what if she panics?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
Yes, it is just so unexpected.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'tell', paired with 'рассказать'.

examples.trans: Yes, just do not tell anyone.
Well, tell me everything!
He's telling a story.

meanings.en: to hurt, to mistreat, to offend
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ижать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'insult', paired with 'обидеть'.

examples.trans: You offend me, Viktor Petrovich.
But hurting children isn't right.
Never hurt little ones.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We will wash everything out quickly.
We will fix everything!
We do not wish you any harm.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A coconut has already fallen on me.
Well, I am completely alive.
Let us make a bet then.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
Hello, Viktor Petrovich.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'lads, guys' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Hello, did my husband stop by here?
You and I are men, after all.
Is there another man in there with you?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real').

examples.trans: We are true keepers of secrets.
That inspector was not real.
This is real success!

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'keepers / guardians' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We are true keepers of secrets.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть хранитель.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always keepers.

meanings.note: Borrowed via French 'secret' from Latin 'secretum' (something set apart or hidden).

examples.trans: We are true keepers of secrets.
That is a big secret.
These are our little men's secrets!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: Nobody is going to die here today!
Today I am covering for you here.
Chef, are you going to win it back today?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'крывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'I cover for', paired with 'прикрыть'.

examples.trans: Today I am covering for you here.

examples.text: Не надо прикрывать своё горе бравадой.
examples.trans: Do not cover up your grief with bravado.

examples.text: Он всегда прикрывает своих друзей в трудную минуту.
examples.trans: He always covers for his friends in a tough moment.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We will wash everything out quickly.
Quickly hold him right here!
Lyova, fly quickly to the bank.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common feminine noun meaning 'little bottle' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Chef, do not throw the bottle away.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть бутылочка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always little bottle.

meanings.en: to throw out, to toss out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брасывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to throw out', paired with 'выбросить'.

examples.trans: Chef, do not throw the bottle away.
Throwing a person out the window is not normal!

examples.text: Иван Васильевич, выбрасывать человека в окно нормально?
examples.trans: Ivan Vasilyevich, is throwing a person out the window normal?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'suddenly, what if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: In case we have to stun someone else.
Why did it suddenly draw level?
Suddenly it began to rain.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Look, he is still right there!
And there came to be even more money.
And I will save up more for myself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to stun / knock out'.

examples.trans: In case we have to stun someone else.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и оглушить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to stun on time.

meanings.en: to have to, to be forced to
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'йтись'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'it will be necessary', paired with 'приходиться'.

examples.trans: I'm going to have to torture you.
We had to wait a long time.

examples.text: Ты что, очкарик, не понимаешь? Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will say', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: You said the wife was on me.
I told you, pull up your pants!
You said to bring him down.
